metrics.note: author: profile of eplb_state.py rearrange on one rank incl. P2P + GPU copies (1s370ms -> 1s77ms); ours: CPU index-mapping path for all 8 ranks x 48 layers, no transport -- compare the ratio, not the absolute

headline: rearrange_e2e

reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine); primitives unquantified by the author ('20-25% on average')

author_hardware_args.text: - Implements `get_ep_ranks_with_expert`, `move_to_buffer`, `move_from_buffer` in numpy which gives 20-25% on average for each primitive

reliability.note: baseline 0.0058 ms < 100 us per call: dominated by host launch/sync latency on this machine; ratio unreliable, absolute meaningless

gap.verdict: workload mismatch (micro-bench regime) + unit label bug
gap.note: Author: 27 % on `rearrange` (1.37 s → 1.08 s) inside a live `-dp 8` Qwen3-Next-80B EPLB rebalance (58 MoE layers × 512 physical experts, real P2P), plus "20-25 % per primitive" unquantified. Ours: three inlined primitives at `NUM_LOCAL=16`: `get_ep_ranks_with_expert` 8.2× faster (consistent with the author), but `move_to_buffer` 0.74× and `move_from_buffer` 0.38× — at 16 local experts the pure-Python body is 16×16 = 256 trivial iterations (23 µs) while the numpy body pays ~10 numpy-call overheads (31 µs); numpy only wins once `num_local_experts` and the per-layer loop are large. The headline/median therefore reports a regression the author never claimed. Also: `bench.py:_best_ms` returns **ms** (`*1e3`) but `task.json` declares `unit: "us"` — every 29499 number on the dashboard is mislabelled by 1000×. To match the author: bench the whole per-layer rebalance (loop over all `ep_rank`s × 58 layers, i.e. the `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace` index-mapping path with `num_local_experts` ≥ 32 as in Qwen3-Next with 32 redundant experts), make `get_ep_ranks_with_expert` or the E2E loop the headline, and fix the unit to `ms`. Verdict: workload, not hardware (CPU-only).
